items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: I said, “but I want to see my little girl”

ctx.x: remember it, when he was making a movie. And I’ve always been a night owl, because he’d always get home at two or three and I’d always wait with him and we’d have breakfast early in the morning and I thought that was hot stuff. And he’d come home. And I heard something about movies, and I knew this, and I started to, my mother, he got up and I jumped up and I got my bag and I had my hat, and I was packing and trying to get ready and putting my shoes on the wrong feet, and Daddy always tells this story much…

She says, “Mother, I see you’re not going. I’m going with Daddy.” She was about three years old. So she says, “I see you’re not going.” And she says, “but I’m going.” So I couldn’t take her though, at that time of morning, because we were making this picture, I don’t know if it was “Hellzapoppin” with Dorothy Dandridge. Anyway, but she wanted to go. She wanted to go everywhere I’d go. And I remember the night she was born, I wanted to see her to visit, and I was working, it was just about the time we were working…

There’s a story I remember traveling with Basie and at that time they traveled on the trains and this is when they had the berth that you could sleep in. And then you’d have, every morning the wives with the kids of all the musicians would come and we’d come to breakfast. And there was Snooky, played the trumpet with Basie at the time, and then Earle Warren, and I’d have names for all of them. Well musicians have names for each other, Smiley, and Sweets —
